The viewer material list is read by pattern matching, so a reformat of the source file could silently change results.

terms.meaning: a list file saying which 3D models exist and their details
a common single-file format for 3D models
the surface look of a part, such as glass or concrete

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared setup and folder paths
sections.what: Sets the project root and the frontend models folder that the other tests in this file read from.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the tests find their files no matter where they are run from.
sections.watch_out: Moving this test file or the models folder breaks these paths.

sections.name: _viewer_material_keys
sections.title: Reads the viewer's allowed material names
sections.what: Reads the viewer's materials source file and collects the names of the materials it defines.
sections.why: Likely reason: so model files are compared against the viewer's real list rather than a copy.
sections.watch_out: It finds names by pattern matching the text, so reformatting that file can make it find no names.

sections.name: _glb_materials
sections.title: Reads material names from a model file
sections.what: Opens a binary 3D model file, reads its embedded JSON section, and returns the material names it uses.
sections.why: Likely reason: material names are stored inside the model file, and this reads them without needing a 3D library.
sections.watch_out: Assumes the standard single-file layout with a JSON section first, so a different file format fails here.

sections.name: test_every_library_model_uses_viewer_materials_and_matches_its_manifest
sections.title: Every library model matches the viewer and manifest
sections.what: For each manifest entry, checks that the model file exists, that every material it uses is known to the viewer, that its native size values are positive, and that any repeat setting uses x, y or z. It also checks that the concrete, glass and water materials exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops models that the viewer cannot colour or position from being shipped.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a material requires changing both the model file and the viewer list, or this fails.

sections.name: test_layouts_only_ask_for_models_that_exist
sections.title: Layout only asks for models that exist
sections.what: Checks that each item kind the layout can produce either has a model in the manifest or appears in a built-in list of shapes drawn by code.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a placed item never points at a model that is missing.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new layout kind needs either a model or an entry in the built-in list in this test.

summary: Tests that every 3D model in the shipped library uses materials the viewer knows, matches its manifest, and is used correctly by the layout code.
purpose: Catches broken or mismatched 3D models before they reach the viewer, where they would show wrong colours or fail to load.
why: Likely reason: the 3D models, the viewer's material list and the layout code are three separate lists that must agree. Reason not stated in the code beyond this.
how: Reads the manifest file, collects the viewer's material names from its source file, opens each model file to read its embedded material names, and compares them. It then checks that every item kind the layout can produce either has a model or is in a built-in list of drawn shapes.
inputs: The manifest JSON file, each model file in the models folder, the viewer materials source file, and the layout module's list of kinds.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. No files are written.
risks: The built-in list of drawn shapes is typed into the test by hand, so it can fall out of step with the layout code and hide a missing model.
debug: Read the failing assertion message, which names the model or layout kind. Check the manifest entry, then the material names in the viewer materials file.
